### `Rendered`  <sub>data</sub>

```
Rendered := Midi Int Int Int
    Perc Int Int
```

A committed, playable event: program, key, velocity.  Concrete because
MIDI is the only backend; this type is the seam where another would go.
`Midi` is a pitched note on some program; `Perc` is an unpitched one.
The distinction is musical, not a transport detail — percussion is a
different *kind* of sound, and which MIDI channel carries it is the
renderer's business (`gestate/midi.py`).


### `Score`  <sub>data</sub>

```
Score a := Note a                # `'x` — unassigned, carries the payload
    Play Rendered         # committed to MIDI: parametric in `a`
    Assigned Voice        # committed to a `voices` bank; likewise
    Rest
    Seq (Score a) (Score a)
    Par (Score a) (Score a)   # `||` — at the same time
    At Int (Score a)
    Scale (Score a) Int
    Shrink (Score a) Int
    Retro (Score a)          # `reverse` — back to front
    Sow Int (Score a)         # `sow n s` — re-root a subtree's seed
    Clip Int (Score a)        # `long n s` — a declared span
    Mark String               # a named point, zero wide
    Draw (Int -> Score a)
    Hear (Chan (List Int)) Int (List Int -> Score a)
    TempoShape (List Tempo) (Score a)
    Shape (Chan Float) (List Envelope) (Score a)
    Fermata (Chan Int)
```


### `ticksPerBeat`

```
ticksPerBeat : Int
```

**Ticks to the beat.**  96 divides by 2,3,4,6,8,12,16,24,32,48, so every
division anyone writes is exact — and the whole score is laid out in
these, so a bar of four is `4 * ticksPerBeat`.

It was `beat`, and the plain word has gone to the *audio* side, where
`beat : Sig Float` is what time it is in beats.  Two things called
"beat" is one too many, and of the two this is the one that is really a
resolution rather than a beat.

### `Semigroup (Score b)`  <sub>instance</sub>

```
instance Semigroup (Score b) where
```

`++` is *music sequence* here, shadowing the core prelude's list append.
A class with two instances would be the general answer and is not needed:
An *instance* rather than a redefinition, which is what stops it hiding
the prelude's list append — see `prelude.ges`, where `++` is now
`Semigroup`'s method.  A music program has both again.

### `Reversible Score`  <sub>instance</sub>

```
instance Reversible Score where
```

**Retrograde** — the phrase backwards, which is the third of the four
things a canon does to a subject.

A *constructor* rather than a walk that turns the tree inside out, and
`||` is why: an overlay is **left-aligned**, so reversing `a || b`
structurally would leave two voices of unequal length still starting
together, when what a retrograde means is that they still *end*
together.  The duration is not known until the subtree is laid out, so
the mirror happens where the duration is — in `layOnto`, against the
events, exactly as `Scale` does.

`reverse` and not `retrograde`, because that is what this operation is
called everywhere else it appears; `prelude.ges` has the class and the
list instance.


### `at`

```
at : Int -> [: a :] -> [: a :]
```

`at` translates a score's *extent* and leaves its *duration* alone, which
is why `a ++ at (-1) b` overlaps `a` without moving what follows.

### `Monad Score`  <sub>instance</sub>

```
instance Monad Score where
```

Substitute a score for each *unassigned* note.  `Play` is left alone —
it carries no payload — which is why "ignored if an instrument is already
selected" needs no runtime mark.
An *instance*, for the reason `++` above is one.  A score's `pure` is
`Note`, which is exactly what `'x` already writes.


### `prog`

```
prog : Int -> Int -> [: b :]
```

**A MIDI program number, as an instrument.**  `melody >>= prog 73`
commits every unassigned note in `melody` to program 73 — a flute.

An instrument is any function from a note's payload to a committed
score, applied with `>>=`; this is the one that names a MIDI program,
and `percussion` is the other.  A score bound with one holds no payload,
so it is parametric and unifies with `Void` — which is what makes it
performable.

Named `prog` and not `instrument` because a composer wants that word:
this file is prepended as *text*, so a piece that defines its own
`instrument` would have collided with the library rather than shadowed
it, and "instrument" is the first thing anyone reaches for when naming
the four voices of a quartet.


### `percussion`

```
percussion : Int -> [: b :]
```

The percussion instrument.  It needs no program number, so it is itself
the function `>>=` wants: `pattern >>= percussion`.

## Tempo


### `Tempo`  <sub>type alias</sub>

```
type Tempo = Envelope
```

**A tempo *is* an envelope** — of beats per minute, against beats — so
this is `audio.ges`'s `Envelope` under the name a piece calls it by,
rather than a second type with the same two constructors.  Declaring it
twice would give a scored program two `Step`s, and a constructor's name
is the whole program's.


## Forever is a value — `spec/dynamicscore.md`, stage two


### `cycle`

```
cycle : [: a :] -> [: a :]
```

`cycle bar` is `bar`, then `cycle bar` — which the lazy machine only
ever builds as far as somebody plays it.  Nothing here is new to the
language; what is new is a performer that stops demanding.


### `unfold`

```
unfold : b -> (b -> ([: a :], b)) -> [: a :]
```

A generative score: `unfold seed next`, where `next` grows one section
and the state the following one grows from.  Seed it and it is
replayable — the transcript records the seed, not the surprise.


### `streamVoices`

```
streamVoices : [: Void :] -> List (Int, Int, Voice)
```

The stream a dynamic performance forces — `layVoices`' twin, an event
list in **beat order, lazy in its tail**, so a performer can force
enough to cover the next few beats and no more.  Like `layVoices` it
is named by a generated entry point (`streamMain`), which is why it
stays above the marker; the walk it fronts is below.


### `liveVoices`

```
liveVoices : [: Void :] -> List Cue
```

The stream a *listening* performance forces — `streamVoices` with one
more power: it can end in a question.  A `CueAsk` is a `hear` reached:
its continuation holds **the entire rest of the performance**, so the
host answers it with the port's reading at the downbeat and simply
keeps walking the list the answer returns.  No rebuilding, no second
walk — the question is the spine, suspended.


## Reading the seed — `spec/dynamicscore.md`, stage three


### `sow`

```
sow : Int -> [: a :] -> [: a :]
```

Re-root a subtree's seed: `sow 7 intro ++ improvisation` is fixed
art inside an improvisation.


### `long`

```
long : Int -> [: a :] -> [: a :]
```

**A declared span: this branch is `n` beats long, whatever its
content does.**  `long 16 verse` pins the verse to sixteen beats —
content past the box is clipped, content short of it rests out the
difference — which is the stage-three invariant handed to the
author: content bends, time doesn't.

The declaration pays twice.  Today it is structure a reader can
trust; next it is what lets a performer *skip*: a branch whose width
is written down can be passed over without forcing what is inside,
so resuming a long-running piece descends by arithmetic instead of
unfolding from the left.  (A listening bar wants one: a question's
own width is unknown until it is answered, so `long 1 (do ks <-
hear p; …)` is what lets a rebuild skip past the bar it stands
in — see `opaqueHead`.)


### `mark`

```
mark : String -> [: a :]
```

**A bar point** — zero beats wide, so `mark 1 ++ verse` moves
nothing.  A mark is a place the music can be re-entered: the
performer enumerates them (`streamMarks`, below with the walks)
without touching a single note, and a resume names one instead of
unfolding everything to its left.  Numbered rather than named,
the way seeds are: what matters is that the same one means the
same place twice.


### `section`

```
section : String -> [: a :] -> [: a :]
```

**A named span** — `section "verse" body` marks where the verse
begins and plays it.  A *point*, not a wrapper: the mark is zero
wide and the body follows it, so a section costs the algebra
nothing and `durOf (section n s)` is `durOf s` by construction.

The idiom this exists for is Henri's — the form of a piece written
as *payloads* and bound to the function that plays them:

    score = ('"opening" ++ '"verse" ++ '"closing") >>= scoreParts

    scoreParts name = section name (case name of
        "opening" -> intro
        "verse" -> verse
        _ -> coda)

Bind preserves the spine exactly, so a position in the form is a
position in the music: that is what makes these names *paths*
rather than decorations, and what lets a transport re-enter by one
(`streamMarks`, `spec/ariadne.md`).


### `tempoShape`

```
tempoShape : List Tempo -> [: a :] -> [: a :]
```

**A tempo, written where it happens.**  `tempoShape` bends the
clock across one subtree's span — a ritardando in the bar it
belongs to, rather than at the top of the file:

    coda = tempoShape [Step 0.0 120.0, Ramp 1.0 60.0] lastBar

The points are the same `Tempo` a piece writes globally — absolute
beats-per-minute — and their beats are **fractions of the span**,
so the shape scales with `|*` and reverses with `reverse` the way
any annotation over a subtree does.

**It is spliced into the piece's one envelope, not integrated.**
`tempo.py` keeps tempo linear in *time* precisely so beat inverts
in closed form, and that inverse is four features (a precomputed
schedule, seek-to-bar, the bar ruler, looping).  A local shape is
therefore a *rewrite* of the global envelope at two computable
beats — one envelope still, still invertible — and never a second
clock integrated forward, which is the shape `music.ges` refused
when it chose an envelope over a `Sig Float` in the first place.


### `shape`

```
shape : Chan Float -> List Envelope -> [: a :] -> [: a :]
```

**A channel written across a span** — a crescendo said where it
happens.  The points' beats are *fractions of the span*, so the
shape scales with `|*` and reverses with `reverse` as any
annotation over a subtree does, and a flat envelope is a knob set
once.  What it writes is automation at control rate, which in
gestate is once per block; smoothing finer than that is `slew`'s
job in signal land.


### `fermata`

```
fermata : Chan Int -> [: a :]
```

**Wait here until the world says go.**  Zero beats wide, like a
mark: what it holds is the *clock*, so the notes already sounding
simply go on sounding — their releases sit at ticks the clock has
not reached — and nothing in the layout moves.  It holds while the
channel reads non-zero and releases when it reads zero, so a pedal,
a knob and a count of held keys all drive it the same way.

It holds for as long as it is held.  There is no ceiling: a fermata
means *wait*, the player is right there, and a transport can always
seek.


### `bar`

```
bar : [: a :]
```

**An anonymous bar point** — `bar ++ verse ++ bar ++ chorus` marks
the seams without naming them.  Anonymity works because a resume
goes to the nearest point by *tick*, never by number; the
enumeration numbers these left to right for a human to point at,
which shifts when marks are added — a place that must keep its
name across edits writes `mark n` instead.


### `Port`  <sub>type alias</sub>

```
type Port = Int
```

**Which reading a `hear` asks for.**  An alias of `Int` for the
reason `Seed` is over in `synth.ges`: the number is an identity the
expander assigns (`holds.<bank>` is port `k` for the `k`-th bank),
and what the name buys is a signature that says which integer is
wanted.


### `draw`

```
draw : [: Int :]
```

**The seed at this position** — ariadne's chance leaf
(`spec/ariadne.md`).  A value, not a span: `do s <- draw; f s` is
`f` of the seed this position carries, to the tick — the sower
eliminates every `Draw` before any walk measures, so the algebra
never notices the draw happened.  N draws are N binds; a walk seeds
itself with `do s <- draw; unfold (mix64 s) step`.  A seed is spent,
not read: the usual next line is `below`, one bounded pick per draw.


### `hear`

```
hear : Chan (List Int) -> [: List Int :]
```

**The world at this instant** — ariadne's listening leaf.  The
reading arrives at the leaf's own downbeat, the content it chooses
carries its own time, and **what follows is placed after whatever
the answer chose** — the one place time is decided by the thread
rather than the text (`spec/ariadne.md`, B7 restated).  Unlike
the surface this replaced, there is no box: a four-beat answer
takes four beats.


### `tempoSpans`

```
tempoSpans : [: Void :] -> List (Int, Int, List Tempo)
```

Every mark and where it falls, `(tick, mark)`, beat-ordered and
lazy — `streamVoices`' little sibling, named by its own generated
entry (`marksMain`), which is why it stands above the marker.
Every `tempoShape` and the span it covers, `(from, to, points)` in
ticks — the piece's own tempo rewrites, enumerated the way marks
are and for the same reason: a host has to know them *before* it
can schedule, and an endless piece must be able to answer for a
prefix.


### `shapeSpans`

```
shapeSpans : [: Void :] -> List (Int, Int, Chan Float, List Envelope)
```

Every `shape` and the span it covers, `(from, to, chan, points)` in
ticks — read the way `tempoSpans` is, and for the same reason: the
host writes the channel and must know where the span is before it
can.


### `streamMarks`

```
streamMarks : [: Void :] -> List (Int, String)
```


### `resumeAt`

```
resumeAt : Int -> [: a :] -> [: a :]
```

**The remainder of a score from tick `t` on** — what a resume plays,
with `t` rebased to zero.  The walk *descends by declared widths*:
a `Clip` whose box ends before `t` is skipped without forcing one
thing inside it, which is what turns resuming a long-running piece
from an unfolding into an arithmetic.  Run on the **sown** tree
(`resumeMain` composes it after `sowScore`), so every surviving
subtree keeps exactly the seed its position always had.

Two honest slops, both bounded by where resumes happen (beat and
bar points): a cut inside `Scale k` floors to the nearest multiple
of `k`, and a cut *into* a retrograde keeps it whole — a mirror has
no remainder that is not also a different piece.


### `opaqueHead`

```
opaqueHead : [: a :] -> Bool
```

**Does this subtree's head hold an unanswered question?**  The one
thing a resume cannot step over: `durOf` of a `Hear` is 0, so the
`Seq` arithmetic below would drop the branch and try the next —
forever, on a `cycle`.  Asking first turns that into a defined
answer (resume *at* the joint) instead of a walk that never
advances.

It terminates where the naive walk does not, and for the reason
worth writing down: it descends into a right sibling **only** when
the left is both measured-as-zero and not itself a question — a
chain of `mark`s, which is finite in any piece — and a declared
`long` answers `False` at once, because a box's width is known
whatever its content does.  That is the idiom this predicate exists
to reward.


### `resumeSeq`

```
resumeSeq : Int -> Int -> [: a :] -> [: a :] -> [: a :]
```

An instance receives a seed it owns outright; what it does not

### `split`

```
split : Int -> (Int, Int)
```

Two independent seeds from one — how randomness travels *into*
ordinary code: thread one half, hand on the other.


### `keyOf`

```
keyOf : Int -> Int
```

A seed narrowed to a **position key** that fits a signed 64-bit
slot.  A seed is 64 unsigned bits and the key travels through two
machines, one of which counts in signed integers (`crust`); one bit
is the whole price, and identity is what the number is for.


### `below`

```
below : Int -> Int -> Int
```

**One draw in `0 .. n-1`** — the standard way a seed becomes a
bounded choice.  `draw`'s usual companion: `do s <- draw` hands the
position its seed, and `below n s` spends it on one uniform pick —
usually an index into a table of figures, which is `moods.ges`'s
whole chancy line (`long 4 (phraseOf (below 4 s))`).  Two
*independent* picks want two seeds (`split`, or a second `draw`);
two `below`s over one seed make correlated choices.


### `roll`

```
roll : (Float -> [: a :]) -> [: a :]
```

`draw`, with the seed already spent on one uniform draw.  The
content's time is its own — ariadne has no box to fit.


### `chance`

```
chance : Float -> [: a :] -> [: a :]
```

Play `s` with probability `p`, else a beat of rest.  (Under the old
boxed surface both arms were clipped alike; ariadne keeps the time
of whichever arm plays, so give the arms equal width yourself when
`s` is wider than a beat.)


### `sowScore`

```
sowScore : Int -> [: a :] -> [: a :]
```

**Where the seed enters the tree** — named by the generated entry
points beside `layVoices` and `streamVoices`, which is why it stays
above the marker.  A score with no `draw` in it passes through
unchanged whatever the seed, which is what keeps fixed art fixed.

#### `placeScaled`

```
placeScaled : Int -> Int -> List (Int, Int, Rendered) -> List (Int, Int, Rendered)
```

Scaling a subtree's events into place: `placeScaled off k es` puts local
coordinate `x` of a scaled subtree at `off + x*k`.  Only `Scale` and `Shrink` need this —
translation composes with the offset `layOnto` already carries, so there
is no `shiftEvents` any more.

These destructure in the lambda rather than projecting: a lambda
parameter's type is not known at a projection site — `map`'s
instantiation settles it later, and projection is resolved from the type
(`fixme.md` F28) — while a pattern needs no such knowledge, which is what
the error message says to do.

#### `flipEnv`

```
flipEnv : List Envelope -> List Envelope
```

An envelope read backwards: each point's fraction mirrored and the
list turned round, so a shape under `reverse` runs backwards over
the reversed content — the law `spec/shape.md` states.

**The flags ride their own points**, which is the one thing a
mirror cannot make exact: `Step` and `Ramp` say what happens on
*arrival*, and arrival changes ends when time does.  A ramp
reversed is a ramp to where it came from, which is what a player
means by it; a step reversed steps at the mirrored place.


#### `flipPoint`

```
flipPoint : Envelope -> Envelope
```


#### `shiftFlags`

```
shiftFlags : List Envelope -> List Envelope
```

**The flags move one place along.**  `Step`/`Ramp` is a property of
the point being *arrived at*, so a segment's slope belongs to its
later end — and reversing time swaps which end that is.  Mirroring
the beats alone left every ramp behind a step, which reads as a
flat line: the whole shape went quiet while looking correct.

```
shiftGo : Bool -> List Envelope -> List Envelope
```

#### `streamMarksTo`

```
streamMarksTo : Int -> Int -> [: a :] -> List (Int, String)
```

The bounded walk a `Clip` needs — and a *filter* cannot be: a markless
endless branch never yields the element the filter is waiting on, so
the bound has to ride the spine and cut it where the offset crosses
the box.  The duplication beside `streamMarksAt` is the `…V` pattern's
again: the same walk with one more fact in hand.


### The unfolding half — `spec/dynamicscore.md`, stage two


#### `durOf`

```
durOf : [: a :] -> Int
```

A score's **duration in ticks, from its shape alone** — no events are
laid to answer it, which is what lets a sequence stream: the right
half's offset needs the left half's duration, not its notes.
The algebra is `layVoicesOnto`'s, separated from the laying: `at`
translates extent and leaves duration alone, an overlay lasts as long
as its longer branch, and every leaf — even a rest — is one beat.


#### `mergeVoices`

```
mergeVoices : List (Int, Int, Voice) -> List (Int, Int, Voice) -> List (Int, Int, Voice)
```

Two beat-ordered streams as one.  **Left-biased** on a shared onset,
which keeps an overlay's branches in writing order at the instant they
coincide — the same order the eager layout gives a stable sort, so the
allocator makes the same choices either way.


#### `streamVoicesAt`

```
streamVoicesAt : Int -> [: a :] -> List (Int, Int, Voice)
```


### The seed arithmetic — SplitMix64, spelled portable


#### `wrap64`

```
wrap64 : Int -> Int
```


#### `xorBits`

```
xorBits : Int -> Int -> Int
```

The primitive, because the fold below cost 64 case-splits per call
and a resume descends through two mix64s *per spine level* — 71
seconds of rejoin were measured before this line.  `xorGo` stays as
the primitive's written-out meaning: what `prim_xor_int` computes,
what `crust`'s `XorInt` is held to, and what either would be checked
against if they ever disagreed.


#### `xorGo`

```
xorGo : Int -> Int -> Int -> Int -> Int
```


#### `mixA`

```
mixA : Int -> Int
```

`z ^ (z >> 30)`, and its two siblings — shifts are division, because
the numbers are kept non-negative by `wrap64` at every entry.


#### `mulWrap`

```
mulWrap : Int -> Int -> Int
```

`(a * b) mod 2^64`, with every intermediate under 2^96.  A full
64×64 product reaches 2^128 − 2^65 — one bit past what a signed
128-bit machine holds — and `crust` refuses it rather than wrap;
the reference never noticed, Python's integers having no width,
which is exactly the kind of fact a second machine exists to
surface.  Split the left factor at 2^32 and reduce the high half
early: bit-identical mod 2^64, so no draw moves.


#### `mixB`

```
mixB : Int -> Int
```

```

```


#### `unit`

```
unit : Int -> Float
```

One uniform draw in 0.0 .. 1.0 — the top 53 bits, which is every bit
a `Float` can hold.


### The live walk — a stream that can end in a question


#### `Cue`  <sub>data</sub>

```
Cue := CueEv Int Int Voice
    CueAsk Int (Chan (List Int)) Int (List Int -> List Cue)
    CueEnd Int
    CueHold Int (Chan Int)
```


#### `spliceEnd`

```
spliceEnd : List Cue -> (Int -> List Cue) -> List Cue
```

Continue a self-terminated stream: walk to its `CueEnd`, hand the
end tick to what follows.  This is `Seq` — and it is why `durOf`
no longer appears in the live walk at all: **the width of a
subtree is a fact its own stream reports**, answers included,
which is what makes a `hear`'s content take exactly the time it
takes (`spec/ariadne.md`, time linearized at the joints).


#### `raiseEnd`

```
raiseEnd : Int -> List Cue -> List Cue
```

The larger of a finished branch's end and whatever the surviving
branch reports — `Par`'s join, where the constant law demands the
overlay be as wide as its widest answered branch.


#### `endAt`

```
endAt : Int -> List Cue -> List Cue
```

A declared box's own end, whatever the content did — `Clip`'s cap.
